title: Eating Lots of Chili Peppers May Raise the Risk of One Deadly Cancer
hook: A major review links heavy chili pepper consumption to a higher risk of esophageal cancer — though it's an association, not proof of cause.
key_points: A major review found that people who ate the most chili peppers had a substantially higher risk of esophageal cancer.
Evidence for a similar link to stomach and colorectal cancers was less clear and less consistent.
Researchers emphasize this shows an association from observational data, not a proven cause-and-effect relationship.
It remains unclear whether moderate, occasional chili consumption carries anything like the same risk as the heaviest intake levels studied.
content_html: Chili peppers are a kitchen staple for billions of people — but a large review of the evidence suggests heavy consumption may come with a real cancer risk.
extra_html: The review found that people who consumed the most chili peppers had a substantially higher risk of esophageal cancer specifically, while evidence linking chili consumption to stomach and colorectal cancers was weaker and less consistent. Importantly, the researchers stress that this is an association uncovered by observational data, not proof that chili peppers directly cause cancer — other lifestyle and dietary factors could be involved. It's also still unclear whether moderate, occasional chili consumption carries anything like the same risk as the heaviest intake levels studied; the researchers say more targeted research is needed to answer that.

flashcards.back_html: Esophageal cancer — people with the highest chili consumption had a substantially higher risk.

flashcards.prompt: Does this review prove that chili peppers cause esophageal cancer?

choices.text: No — it shows an association from observational data, not proof of cause and effect
Yes, the review used controlled experiments proving causation
No — the review actually found no link at all

flashcards.explanation_html: Researchers explicitly caution that observational associations like this don't establish causation — other lifestyle or dietary factors could be involved.

flashcards.prompt: What remains unclear from this research?
flashcards.back_html: Whether moderate, occasional chili consumption carries a similar risk to the heaviest intake levels studied — more research is needed to know.
